item.title: NPA boss seeks regional port cooperation to cut cargo costs
item.description: By Godwin Oritse President of the Port Management Association of West and Central Africa (PMAWCA), Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, has called for stronger regional cooperation among ports to reduce cargo clearance delays, lower logistics costs and boost intra-African trade. Dantsoho, who is also Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), made the call at the association’s 46th Annual Council and Joint Gulf of Guinea Commission-PMAWCA Forum in Malabo, Equatorial Guinea. He urged port authorities to prioritise strategic collaboration over unhealthy competition, identifying prolonged cargo dwell time, high port charges, expensive transport corridors and poor interoperability among customs systems as major obstacles to regional trade. He noted that the challenges particularly affected landlocked countries, including Mali, Niger, Chad and Burkina Faso, which depend on coastal ports for international trade. Dantsoho also identified geopolitical disruptions, climate change, cyber threats and emerging maritime decarbonisation regulations as challenges requiring urgent collective action by regional port authorities. He called for increased investment in modern port infrastructure, digital security, green port initiatives and the blue economy, including ship repair, sustainable fishing and clean marine fuels. Warning against the implications of failing to adapt to changing global shipping regulations, he said the energy transition could reshape international shipping routes and port calls. “Moreover, the maritime decarbonisation regulations currently taking shape at the International Maritime Organization will soon redraw global shipping routes and ports of call: any port that fails to prepare for this energy transition risks being bypassed altogether. “Finally, rapid digitalisation, while indispensable, exposes our operations to sophisticated cyber threats that we can no longer afford to underestimate,” he said. The PMAWCA president urged member ports to develop clear implementation roadmaps and strengthen accountability, proposing that progress on agreed resolutions be presented at the association’s 47th Annual Council. Also speaking, Executive Secretary of the Gulf of Guinea Commission, Mr Jose Mba Abeso, called for stronger maritime security cooperation to combat illegal fishing, drug and human trafficking, as well as protect critical offshore infrastructure, including subsea cables and gas pipelines. Similarly, Equatorial Guinea’s Minister of Environment and Blue Economy, Mr Fidel Esono Mba Eyono, stressed the importance of sustainable exploitation of marine resources, warning against pollution, illegal fishing and other activities threatening marine ecosystems. item.title: INEC debunks claims of remote BVAS log-out, result loss
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has dismissed claims that its Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) can be remotely logged out before voting concludes. The commission described the claims as false and misleading in a clarification issued on Tuesday through its official X account. INEC was responding to a viral Instagram video alleging that officials could remotely log out voters from BVAS before voting ended. The commission described the video as fabricated and misleading, urging Nigerians to disregard its claims about the system’s operation. “For the avoidance of doubt, the commission wishes to clarify the operational procedures of the BVAS and the process for uploading polling unit results to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV),” it stated. According to INEC, each polling unit receives unique login credentials, which are issued to the presiding officer on the eve of an election. The credentials enable the official to access BVAS for voter accreditation and subsequently upload the polling unit result sheet after voting. “The claim that the BVAS can be remotely logged out before the conclusion of accreditation and voting is false,” the commission stated. It explained that only the poll official operating the device could log in or log out during accreditation or result uploading. “There is no provision for remote log-out by any external individual or authority,” INEC added. The commission also dismissed claims that election results uploaded offline could be lost. It said the IReV application was upgraded after the 2023 general election to incorporate an offline uploading capability. INEC recalled that some election officials were held hostage at polling units during the 2023 elections because poor connectivity prevented result uploads. It explained that the upgrade allows officials in areas with poor or no network coverage to upload results offline before stakeholders. “The uploaded result sheet remains securely stored on the BVAS pending successful transmission,” the commission stated. It added that results were automatically transmitted to IReV once the device regained internet connectivity. This happens as officials proceed from their polling units to ward collation centres, without requiring further manual intervention. INEC assured Nigerians that BVAS and IReV operate under established procedures designed to protect electoral integrity, transparency and credibility. It urged the public to disregard the viral video and avoid creating or sharing unverified information. The commission advised Nigerians to rely exclusively on its official communication channels for accurate information. “INEC remains committed to transparency, accountability and the conduct of free, fair and credible elections,” it stated. item.title: Pension fund assets hit N31.8trn, as 350,000 Nigerians join scheme
item.description: By Rosemary Iwunze Nigeria’s pension industry recorded an asset growth of more than N4 trillion in eight months to August 2026, as total assets under management stood at N31.8 trillion by August 2026. The sharp increase was buoyed by strong equity market performance, investment returns as well as increase in the number of contributors, with approximately 350,000 new Retirement Savings Account (RSA) registrations recorded during the period. The Executive Secretary/Chief Executive Officer, CEO, of the Pension Fund Operators Association of Nigeria, PenOp, Mrs. Anthonia Ifeanyi-Okoro, disclosed this yesterday during the 2026 Annual Media Retreat held virtually. According to her, the continuous increase in subscriber base is attributable to increased awareness and enforcement of the scheme in both public and private sectors of the nation’s economy. Ifeanyi-Okoro said: “Pension assets under management had climbed to N31.8 trillion as of August 2026, reflecting the industry’s strongest growth momentum in recent years and reinforcing its expanding role in Nigeria’s financial system. “The industry also recorded growth in its membership base, with approximately 11.3 million RSA holders, as efforts to deepen pension participation and strengthen retirement savings continued.” Ifeanyi-Okoro attributed the expansion to improved investment performance, increased contributor enrollment and the gradual diversification of pension fund portfolios. She noted that the equities market recorded a bullish performance during the first two quarters of 2026, contributing positively to pension fund returns. Also speaking, Head of Branding and Communications of PenOp’s Executive Committee, Adeola Oyegbade, identified the performance of the equities market and the entry of new contributors as important drivers of pension asset growth. She disclosed that, approximately, 350,000 Nigerians registered under the pension scheme during the period, adding that, the increase in contributors complemented investment returns in driving the industry’s asset expansion. Oyegbade also explained that the industry’s declining exposure to Federal Government securities was part of a deliberate investment diversification strategy and should not be interpreted as a loss of confidence in government instruments. Ifeanyi-Okoro had earlier disclosed that pension fund allocation to Federal Government securities declined from about 65 per cent at the end of 2025 to 55.9 per cent as of August 2026, as operators increased exposure to other investment opportunities. item.title: YPP presidential hopeful unveils plan to cut governance cost
item.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — The presidential candidate of the Young Progressives Party (YPP), Arc. Peter Agada, has unveiled a governance model, tagged LabourDirect, which he said would reduce the cost of governance through direct labour, lower infrastructure costs and the elimination of contract inflation and financial leakages. Agada unveiled the initiative on Tuesday during the flag-off of his presidential campaign and the presentation of his manifesto in Abuja. Describing LabourDirect as the centrepiece of his proposed administration, he said it was designed to replace inflated contracts with a more transparent and cost-effective system of delivering public infrastructure. He said, “Today, we do not just launch a campaign. We launch a movement, we flag off a new Nigeria. “I stand before you to unveil my manifesto. Not a manifesto of promises. A manifesto of numbers. A manifesto of infrastructure. A manifesto of accountability. My manifesto is called LabourDirect.” The YPP candidate identified the high cost of governance as a major factor contributing to Nigeria’s economic challenges, arguing that excessive spending on roads, buildings, electricity and water infrastructure leaves insufficient resources for education, healthcare and job creation. He said Nigeria’s population, currently estimated at approximately 245 million, was projected to rise to 305 million in 10 years and 365 million in 20 years. Agada also put the country’s Gross Domestic Product at $386.67 billion, while claiming that 154 million Nigerians, representing 63 per cent of the population, were living in multidimensional poverty. “We are growing, but we are getting poorer. This is a jobless boom,” he said. On the country’s debt burden, Agada said public debt stood at ₦166.79 trillion as of June 30, 2026, while debt servicing consumed ₦15.52 trillion, representing 45.2 per cent of government revenue. He argued that the amount spent servicing debt had significantly reduced the resources available for critical public services. “We spend ₦15.52 trillion, 45.2 per cent of all our revenue, just to service debt. Almost half of everything we earn goes to pay old debts. That is why we have no money for schools, hospitals, and roads,” he said. Explaining the LabourDirect model, Agada said it would eliminate unnecessary intermediaries, ghost workers and inflated contracts, thereby reducing the cost of executing government projects. Using road construction as an example, he claimed that while the government spends about ₦2.5 billion to construct one kilometre of road, his model could deliver the same distance for between ₦375 million and ₦500 million. “I stand here today on a road that I built. Not with government money. Not with a loan. With LabourDirect. “The government standard rate for a road like this is ₦2.5 billion per kilometre. I built this road for a fraction of that,” he said. item.title: FG targets $9.3bn care economy, woos private investors
item.description: IFC push investment as Lagos develops care policy framework By Peter Egwuatu The Federal Government is targeting a $9.3 billion care economy as it moves to attract private sector investment into childcare, elderly care and disability support services. The initiative follows the Federal Executive Council’s approval of the National Care Policy and Implementation Plan 2026–2030, aimed at transforming the sector into an organised industry capable of creating millions of jobs and increasing women’s participation in the economy. Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Hajiya Imaan Suleiman-Ibrahim, disclosed this yesterday in Lagos at the National Care Economy Forum hosted by the World Bank Group. She was represented by the Director, Child Development Department, Ali Andrew Maduga. “Our task is to move beyond recognising care as a social responsibility to establishing it as an organised, productive and investable component of Nigeria’s economy,” she said. She disclosed that the Council, on October 28, 2026, also directed the Ministers of Justice and Women Affairs to develop an executive bill to provide legislative backing for the policy. Citing UN Women’s 2026 care economy modelling, she said closing unpaid care gaps and expanding universal childcare could contribute at least $9.3 billion to Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product and generate between 9.4 million and 17 million jobs. She added that caregiving responsibilities accounted for 20.16 per cent of women’s withdrawal from the labour force, compared with 0.6 per cent for men. Earlier, Head of Office, Nigeria, International Finance Corporation (IFC), Christian Mulamula, described care as economic infrastructure rather than merely a family responsibility. “Care may begin at home, but its impact does not end at the front door. It shapes whether people, particularly women, can take up opportunities and participate fully in the economy. “Care is economic infrastructure,” he said. He disclosed that 92 per cent of childcare facilities were small, independently owned businesses, while 76 per cent of childcare entrepreneurs lacked access to formal finance. “Investing in childcare is about freeing talent and productivity into the economy while giving children a strong start in life,” he added. Meanwhile, Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, represented by Commissioner for Finance, Abayomi Oluyomi, said the state was developing an investment-oriented care policy framework. “We want a care economy in which families can access reliable and affordable services, care providers can operate viable businesses, and those who work in the sector can earn decent livelihoods under appropriate professional standards,” he said. Sanwo-Olu urged financial institutions, employers and private investors to support the sector, noting that government funding alone could not provide the required facilities and services. item.title: FG moves to strengthen foreign missions, boost economic diplomacy
item.description: By Favour Ulebor ABUJA—The Federal Government has announced plans to strengthen Nigeria’s foreign missions, improve consular services and make diplomacy more focused on attracting investment, promoting trade and supporting economic growth. The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Sola Enikanolaiye, disclosed this in a statement, yesterday, by his Special Assistant on Digital Media and Public Diplomacy, Raphael Oni, following the opening of the sixth Foreign Policy School (FPS-6) in Abuja. The programme, organised by the Nigerian Institute of International Affairs, NIIA, and the Peace-Building Development Consult, PBDC, is being held from November 16 to 18, 2026, at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Tafawa Balewa House, Abuja. The event, themed “Foreign Policy as a Tool for National Security and Economic Growth,” focuses on how Nigeria can use diplomacy to strengthen national security, attract economic opportunities and promote its interests internationally. Speaking at the opening ceremony, Enikanolaiye said Nigeria’s foreign policy must be built on a strong domestic foundation to achieve meaningful results abroad. He explained that the administration of President Bola Tinubu was introducing reforms within the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to improve its operations and ensure that Nigerian missions abroad delivered measurable results. According to him, the government’s foreign policy is guided by the four Ds: Demography, development, diaspora and democracy, with the welfare and interests of Nigerians at the centre. He noted that the approach didn’t reduce Africa’s importance in Nigeria’s foreign policy but recognised that the country must strengthen its economy and institutions to play a more effective role on the continent. The minister recalled that the ministry adopted the motto “Nigeria First” in 2007, adding that the present administration was working to give it practical meaning. He said Nigerian missions abroad would be repositioned as centres for trade, investment and technology partnerships, while also improving consular services for citizens living overseas. He said: “We are moving beyond the mantra of diplomacy for diplomacy’s sake to a purposeful engagement calibrated to serve our people.” Enikanolaiye also announced three measures to improve accountability and performance across Nigerian missions. He identified them as the Stations Charter, which assigns specific priorities to each mission; SCAPER, an annual performance assessment for Heads of Mission; and the Global Best Practices Project, which will enable missions identify successful policies and practices that could benefit Nigeria. He explained that the measures would ensure that diplomatic activities produced practical results rather than focus only on meetings and engagements. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 18, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian naira opened trading on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, under sustained demand pressure across both the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the parallel market, with the gap between the two segments widening further. At the official window, data published by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) shows that the naira closed the previous session on Tuesday, November 17, at a volume-weighted NFEM rate of ₦1,358.09 per dollar. During Tuesday’s official trading session, the local currency opened at ₦1,355.80 per dollar and fluctuated between an intraday high of ₦1,354.00 and a low of ₦1,364.50 before settling at ₦1,363.00 at the close. Meanwhile, live international interbank spot tracking early Wednesday morning hovered around ₦1,351.25 per dollar. In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, the naira traded significantly weaker. Street dealers and Bureau de Change (BDC) operators in Lagos and Abuja quoted the US dollar at an average of ₦1,440 per dollar early Wednesday morning, with buying and selling rates ranging between ₦1,435 and ₦1,445 per dollar. Based on the latest official NFEM rate of ₦1,358.09 and the parallel market average of ₦1,440.00, the spread between the official and unofficial markets currently stands at approximately ₦81.91 per dollar. Market analysts note that the persistent divergence between both windows reflects heightened seasonal import demand, corporate foreign exchange obligations, and a slowdown in autonomous dollar inflows. Recent market intelligence indicates that while Nigeria’s external reserves slipped slightly by roughly $390 million from their late-October peak of $55.26 billion due to central bank market interventions, the reserve buffer remains over 26 percent higher than the $43.54 billion recorded during the same period in 2025. Financial analysts expect the Central Bank of Nigeria to maintain liquidity support in the official NFEM window to keep official rates anchored near the ₦1,350 to ₦1,365 band, even as retail and unfulfilled demand continues to exert upward pressure on parallel market quotes. item.title: Atiku, Barau, Ikeja LG boss mourn Vanguard Editor, Femi Ajasa
item.description: By Henry Umoru & Olasunkanmi Akoni ABUJA — Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau Jibrin, and Chairman of Ikeja Local Government Area of Lagos State, Akeem Dauda, have mourned the death of Vanguard Newspapers’ Online Editor, Mr Olufemi Ajasa. Ajasa died on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH), after a brief illness. He was aged 44. His death was announced by the management of Vanguard Media Limited, publishers of Vanguard Newspapers. In a condolence message posted on his X handle on Tuesday, Atiku described Ajasa’s death as a painful loss to the journalism profession and Vanguard Media Limited. The African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate said the late editor’s death was a reminder of how suddenly a life devoted to work, family and service could be cut short. He said, “Ajasa’s passing is a deep loss to @vanguardngrnews and to the journalism profession. Behind every story published and every deadline met is a commitment to keeping the public informed. “His colleagues have lost a valued teammate, the media community a respected professional, and his family a beloved son, husband, father and brother.” Atiku extended his condolences to the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, the newspaper’s Editor, Eze Anaba, and the deceased’s family, friends and colleagues. He prayed that the memories Ajasa left behind would comfort his loved ones and that God would grant them the strength to bear the loss. Similarly, Senator Barau described Ajasa as a thoroughbred professional and one of the finest minds in Nigeria’s digital journalism space. In a condolence message issued by his spokesperson, Ismail Mudashir, the Deputy Senate President said Ajasa’s dedication to truth and accuracy distinguished him in the profession. He said, “Femi Ajasa’s dedication and commitment to truth and accuracy set him apart and distinguished him among others. His death is a painful loss, not only to his immediate family, the Vanguard family, but to the entire Nigerian media industry.” Barau recalled that Ajasa began his journalism career as a photojournalist with National Mirror in 2012 before working with TheNewsGuru and Pulse. He later returned to Vanguard in June 2022 as Online Editor, a position in which he distinguished himself through professionalism and commitment to the journalism profession. The senator extended his condolences to the Ajasa family of Ajido, Badagry, Lagos State, the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, the journalism union, friends and professional associates of the deceased. He prayed that God would grant the bereaved family, colleagues and loved ones the strength to bear the loss and grant the deceased eternal rest. Also mourning, Ikeja Local Government Chairman, Akeem Dauda, described Ajasa’s death as a painful loss to the media industry and the journalism profession. item.title: Oil production rises 6.2% to 1.615m bpd, Dangote supply jumps 25%
item.description: •Pipeline outages, terminal delays hamper output By Ediri Ejoh Nigeria’s average daily crude oil and condensate production rose by 6.2 per cent to 1.615 million barrels per day (bpd) in 2025, from 1.521 million bpd in 2024, while crude oil supplied to Dangote Refinery increased by 25.3 per cent to 94.44 million barrels. The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) disclosed this in its 2025 Financial and Operational Performance Report, released at the weekend. The report showed that crude oil production, excluding condensates, increased by 12.6 per cent to 1.475 million bpd in 2025, from 1.310 million bpd in the preceding year. Companies operating under Joint Venture (JV) arrangements and those in land terrains accounted for the largest shares of national production. A breakdown of monthly output showed that production peaked at 1.701 million bpd in July and 1.688 million bpd in June, while the lowest output of 1.521 million bpd was recorded in December. Providing details of production performance, the commission stated: “Reconciled crude oil produced was 589,600,527 barrels (538,696,941 barrels of oil and 50,903,586 barrels of condensate). The daily average production figure was 1,615,344 barrels per day (1,475,882 barrels of oil per day and 139,462 barrels of condensate per day).” It also disclosed that 48 Field Development Plans (FDPs) were approved during the year to develop about 1,751.15 million stock tank barrels of oil reserves, 104.48 million stock tank barrels of condensate reserves and 8.19 trillion cubic feet of gas reserves. However, pipeline outages, planned maintenance and terminal operational challenges constrained production during the year. The commission identified the Trans-Niger Pipeline (TNP), Nembe Creek Trunk Line (NCTL) and Trans Forcados Pipeline (TFP) among the major pipelines affected by outages. “The most prevalent cause during the year was outages of key pipelines (TNP, NCTL, and TFP),” the report stated. It added that “planned maintenance and vessel/tanker loading delays at terminals, which led to the shut-in of wells, also contributed significantly to the deferred volumes.” Meanwhile, crude oil supplied to Dangote Refinery rose to 94.436 million barrels in 2025, from 75.391 million barrels in 2024, representing an increase of 25.3 per cent. In a related development, the NUPRC last week reported that Nigeria’s average daily crude oil and condensate production declined by 1.7 per cent to 1.68 million bpd in October 2026, from 1.71 million bpd in September. Despite the decline, Nigeria met its Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) crude oil production quota for the sixth consecutive month. Crude oil output, excluding condensates, averaged 1.51 million bpd, representing 101 per cent of the country’s 1.5 million bpd quota. item.title: APC shuts down Umuahia for Tinubu
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The All Progressives Congress, APC, on Monday, shut down Umuahia, the Abia State capital, as it formally flagged off its campaign for the 2027 general elections, with a massive rally that drew party leaders, candidates and supporters from across the state. The Umuahia Township Stadium, venue of the rally, was filled to capacity, while heavy vehicular and human traffic disrupted movement around adjoining streets as thousands of party faithful struggled to access the venue. Leading the charge, Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, declared that Abia would deliver 75 per cent of its votes to Tinubu in 2027, insisting that the President would not have to beg for the constitutionally required 25 per cent in the state. Kalu said APC had about 162,000 members in Abia and that the party had challenged each member to mobilise 10 additional voters for Tinubu. According to him, such mobilisation would translate into over 1.6 million votes for the President. “Don’t beg for 25 per cent. Your sons and daughters in Abia State will give you 75 per cent. We have about 2.3 million voters in Abia State. We are mobilising. We are not sleeping,” he declared. He challenged those questioning APC’s electoral strength in Abia to wait for the party’s planned rally at Enyimba Stadium, Aba, on December 7, insisting that the Umuahia rally, organised within one week, was only a foretaste of what was coming. He said the President had demonstrated commitment to the region by addressing longstanding grievances dating back to the Nigerian Civil War. Kalu, who acknowledged the contributions of the President to the establishment of the SEDC, said the commission’s interventions would soon begin to translate into visible development across the five South-East states. He also commended the President for supporting his emergence as Deputy Speaker, describing the position as an opportunity to advance the interests of the region. item.title: Car washer steals customer’s SUV
item.description: By Alumona Ukwueze ENUGU—A 36-year-old car washer, Pius, has been sentenced to seven years’ imprisonment for stealing a customer’s Toyota Lexus 330 SUV in Enugu State. The Enugu State Police Command disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday by its Police Public Relations Officer, SP Daniel Ndukwe. According to the statement, Pius stole the black Lexus SUV on November 5, 2026, after it was entrusted to him by its owner for washing at Fourth Dimension, Enugu. Rather than wash and return the vehicle, the convict, a native of Ugep in Yakurr Local Government Area of Cross River State, allegedly absconded with it and fled to his hometown. Following a complaint by the vehicle’s owner, operatives of the New Haven Police Division deployed technical intelligence to track down and arrest him in Cross River State. The stolen SUV was subsequently recovered on November 11, 2026. The police said Pius was arraigned before the Enugu North Magistrate Court on November 16, 2026, on a one-count charge of stealing. He pleaded guilty to the charge and was convicted and sentenced to seven years’ imprisonment by the court. The Command commended the operatives involved in the investigation and arrest, as well as the court for the speedy dispensation of justice. It reiterated its commitment to sustaining efforts to rid Enugu State of criminal elements and ensure the safety of residents and their property. item.title: Court adjourns divorce case of Gov Yusuf, wife to Dec 15
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – An Upper Area Court sitting in the Gudu District of Abuja, yesterday, fixed December 15, to hear the divorce case involving Governor Abba Yusuf of Kano State and his estranged wife, Zainab. Trial judge, Ado Muktar, deferred hearing of the suit, to enable the parties to file and exchange the necessary processes. While the Kano State Commissioner for Information, Sanusi Bature, appeared for the governor, the plaintiff, Zainab, was represented by her lawyer, Aliyu Baba. Bature told the court that he had received service of the processes on behalf of the governor. He requested an adjournment to enable him to properly brief Governor Yusuf and his legal team on the matter. The application for an adjournment was not opposed by the plaintiff. Speaking to journalists after the proceedings, Bature said he became aware of the case after hearing reports that a matter involving the governor had been filed before the court. He said: “Since the court fixed today for mention, I came to inform the court that I had not been able to brief him on the service I collected. He will have to decide on the next course of action.” However, the Kano State commissioner urged members of the public to exercise restraint in commenting on the matter, which he described as personal and sub judice. “This is a personal matter, so, I want to exercise some level of restraint because it concerns him personally and is also before the court. We do not want to overflog an issue that is already before the court. “We have to remain very neutral in issues like this because they involve families. There are many other stories that are newsworthy, rather than focusing on sensational issues like this,” he added. Zainab, who is the second wife of Governor Yusuf, is the adopted daughter of a former governor of the state and Vice Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso. She approached the court for the dissolution of the marriage, which produced six children, over “irreconcilable differences.” The plaintiff offered to refund the dowry that was paid on her by the governor. The divorce case comes amid a prolonged political fallout between Governor Yusuf and his former political mentor, Senator Kwankwaso, who was instrumental to his ascension to power. Governor Yusuf, while addressing pensioners at the Government House in Kano on Monday, confirmed his marital issues. item.title: Courts must stop deciding election winners — Justice Adefope-Okojie
item.description: By Innocent Anaba LAGOS — FORMER Judge of the Court of Appeal, Justice Oludotun Adefope-Okojie, yesterday, warned Nigerian courts against installing candidates voters rejected through judicial rulings. She noted that “a number of the people in the legislature, not only at federal but at state and local government levels are not the desire of the electorate. They, in consequence, owe the electorate no duty to represent them. This is an aberration.” Justice Adefope-Okojie, who retired from the bench of the Court of Appeal in 2023, also cautioned political parties to comply with the tenets of justice and to observe their various party constitutions in their selection of candidates, to avoid such cases ending up in court. Speaking on the topic ‘Electoral Process in Nigeria: Managing the boundaries of judicial intervention,’ at the GAVEL International Annual Lecture, in Lagos, Justice Adefope-Okojie said: “The credibility of an electoral system depends not only on the conduct of elections but also on the existence of effective mechanisms for resolving disputes arising before, during, and after elections. “The ideal situation should be that the vote of the people should be decided at the polling unit, rather than the court of law. The contrary is, however, the prevalent situation in this country. The political parties have done immeasurable harm to the polity. “They seem incapable of abiding by their own party’s Constitution in their selection of the rightful candidates to be fielded in the election, which, contrarily, in a number of instances has boomeranged against them, with the rightfully elected but rejected candidate working for the opposing side in the actual election, out of spite. “The parties have also taken advantage of the courts’ position of not intervening in the domestic affairs of the party, to commit all manner of atrocities. “It is the flawed congresses and wrongful substitution of successful candidates by imposition of handpicked ones, and an electoral system challenged by honesty, that led to most of the litigations in the past elections. “At the actual election were accusations of ballot snatching, vote rigging, vote buying, manipulations and outright falsification of results. The resultant effect is the recourse to the courts for determination of the rightful candidate, a duty which should have been resolved at the polling booth and the rightful declaration by INEC. “The unfortunate result is that a number of the people in the legislature, not only at federal but at state and local government levels are not the desire of the electorate. They, in consequence, owe the electorate no duty to represent them. This is an aberration. “The simplistic answer to the avoidance or reduction of judicial intervention in electoral matters is for the parties to comply with the tenets of justice and to observe their various party constitutions in their selection of candidates. item.title: 2027: Don’t sacrifice Nigeria’s unity on altar of ambition, Jonathan warns politicians
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike & Chidinma Chukwu ABUJA — Former President Goodluck Jonathan has warned political leaders against allowing their quest for power to tear apart Nigeria’s unity, cautioning that political intolerance, ethnic rivalry and electoral violence could plunge the country into crisis, ahead of the 2027 general elections. He expressed concern over the growing resort to political thuggery and the use of young people as instruments of violence. He also insisted that political competition must not become a threat to national cohesion and peaceful coexistence. Jonathan spoke at the third edition of the Peace and Security Conference, organised by the Goodluck Jonathan Foundation in Abuja, with theme, ‘’Safeguarding Peace and Strengthening Social Cohesion in a Competitive Political Environment.’’ He warned: “We must never allow political ambition to undermine the bonds that hold us together as one nation and in our states.’’ The former President also raised concerns over controversies surrounding judicial pronouncements, particularly conflicting decisions by courts of coordinate jurisdiction, and warned that they could erode public confidence in the judiciary and encourage citizens to resort to self-help. “When citizens begin to lose faith in the courts and resort to self-help, the consequences can be disastrous. The descent from a loss of confidence in institutions to anarchy is a danger we must collectively prevent,” he said. He urged political actors to respect opposing views and recognise the legitimate right of others to contest for political power, while calling on Nigerians to prioritise competence, national interest and service over prejudice and personal ambition when choosing their leaders. In his remarks, chairman of Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan, threatened legal action against political parties, candidates and their supporters who engaged in violence, intimidation and inflammatory campaigns ahead of the elections. Represented by National Commissioner, May Agbamuche-Mbu, the INEC chair said competitive politics naturally involved vigorous debate, sharp differences and passionate mobilisation, but warned that these must not degenerate into violence or lawlessness. He also cautioned against harassment, intimidation and physical attacks on INEC officials and ad hoc election workers, insisting that offenders would face legal consequences. He said: “I must sound a stern warning against any form of harassment, intimidation, or physical attack directed at the leadership, staff, or ad hoc workers of INEC by supporters of any political party—whether within Nigeria or abroad. “Election officials are public servants discharging a sacred constitutional duty; assaulting or threatening them is an assault on the Nigerian state and will be met with decisive legal consequences.” Amupitan identified misinformation, disinformation, artificial intelligence-generated content, deepfake videos and cloned voices as

item.title: Ibom Seaport: All promises, no action
item.description: The Ibom Deep Seaport project is a depressing illustration of Nigeria’s penchant for recycling development promises without delivering results. Conceived in 1999 under the visionary administration of Governor Victor Attah as the Ibaka Deep Seaport and Industrial City, it has survived the regimes of Godswill Akpabio, Udom Emmanuel and the incumbent, Umo Eno, without progressing to actual construction. More than a quarter of a century later, it remains a political talking point rather than an economic reality. Successive governments have offered assurances, raised expectations and announced milestones. The late President Muhammadu Buhari’s administration reportedly secured the Federal Executive Council’s approval for the first phase in December 2020, which is a public-private partnership estimated to cost $4.6 billion and a preferred consortium involving Bolloré Africa Logistics and PowerChina. Yet, that approval did not translate into construction. President Bola Tinubu also promised the project during his 2023 presidential campaign in Uyo. His November 6, 2026 visit to Akwa Ibom, during which he again announced its approval, therefore sounds like a recycled promise. What happened to Buhari’s approval? Why was the preferred investor consortium unable to commence work? Were financing arrangements concluded? What exactly has Tinubu approved that was not approved in 2020? Where are the concession agreements, financial commitments, construction contracts and commencement dates? Nigerians deserve documentary answers. Enough of presidential declarations at political rallies. The reluctance of successive Federal Governments to activate this project is particularly troubling. Nigeria urgently needs to diversify its maritime infrastructure beyond the congested Lagos ports and the struggling facilities elsewhere. Ibom offers an exceptional opportunity. Its proposed deepwater facilities, with an approach channel exceeding 18 metres in depth, could accommodate large ocean-going vessels. Its container, bulk and liquid-cargo terminals, supported by a proposed 14,400-hectare industrial city, could transform regional commerce, manufacturing, agriculture and exports. The economic benefits are enormous: employment, foreign investment, expanded government revenue, cheaper logistics and improved access to international markets. Akwa Ibom could become a major maritime and industrial gateway serving the entire South-East, South-South, North Central, North East and neighbouring countries. Governor Eno must, however, move beyond political lobbying and demand an enforceable implementation timetable. Senate President Godswill Akpabio should deploy his influence to secure federal action. item.title: Nvidia: ‘I’d Be Honoured To Return,’ Jensen Huang On Possible Reinstatement
item.description: Former Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang has said he would be willing to return to the position if the company’s board of directors considers his reinstatement to be in its best interest. Huang made the announcement in a statement posted on his X account on Tuesday, his first public comments since stepping down on November 12, following revelations about alleged extramarital affairs and concerns over his personal conduct. The former chief executive said he had received an outpouring of support from Nvidia employees, investors, business partners and customers, with many urging him to return amid the company’s ongoing challenges. “Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” he wrote. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO.” Huang, however, acknowledged that his personal conduct had fallen short of the standards expected of the company’s leadership and expressed regret over the difficulties his actions had created for the board. “I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret,” he said. “I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.” (FILES) Jensen Huang, co-founder and CEO of Nvidia Corp., speaks during a news conference in Taipei on May 21, 2025. US tech giant Nvidia said on July 14 it will resume sales of its H20 artificial intelligence chips to China, after exports were halted due to US licensing curbs. (Photo by I-Hwa Cheng / AFP) | I-Hwa Cheng / AFP His resignation followed reports of alleged extramarital relationships, including one involving an executive of Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed International, which is under US criminal investigation over allegations that it helped Chinese companies obtain advanced Nvidia artificial intelligence chips in violation of American export controls. The allegations have also drawn attention to Nvidia’s role in the global artificial intelligence industry and concerns over the possible diversion of advanced US technology to China. The controversy has weighed on Nvidia’s shares, adding to uncertainty surrounding the company, which until recently was the world’s most valuable publicly traded company. Huang’s possible return has attracted support from prominent figures in the technology industry, including billionaire entrepreneur Elon Musk and other artificial intelligence investors. An online petition calling for his reinstatement has reportedly attracted more than 190,000 signatures. US President Donald Trump also expressed support for Huang’s return on Monday. item.title: Presidential Election: We Were Blindsided In Lagos In 2023 – Fashola
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor and former Minister of Works, Babatunde Raji Fashola, has said the All Progressives Congress (APC) was caught off guard by its defeat in Lagos during the 2023 presidential election. That outcome is one he says the party is “working tooth and nail” to avoid in 2027. Speaking in an interview on Politics Today, Fashola said the APC never anticipated losing Lagos, the political base of President Bola Tinubu, to the Labour Party candidate Peter Obi. “We were blindsided in Lagos,” Fashola said on Tuesday during an interview on Politics Today. FILE PHOTO: Former Minister of Works, Babatunde Fashola. The former governor, however, argued that the result reflected the growing maturity of Nigeria’s democracy rather than a collapse of the APC’s influence in Lagos. According to him, electoral victories and defeats are part of democratic competition, and political loyalties can shift over time depending on prevailing circumstances. Drawing a football analogy, Fashola said political parties, like football clubs, do not win every match and must constantly adapt to changing realities. “In an election, sometimes you can’t win everywhere. Most times, you can’t win everywhere,” he said. Fashola explained that in previous elections, the APC had strategically redirected its efforts to regions that were becoming more receptive to the party. He suggested that a similar approach would be adopted as the ruling party prepares for the next general election. “It remains to be seen whether, as happened in 2023, Lagos flipped, whether Lagos will flip back,” he said. “And we’re working tooth and nail to ensure that we take back what we lost.” Although he said the party was blindsided in the 2023 presidential election, Fashola dismissed suggestions that Tinubu had been politically “demystified” by the defeat, insisting that opponents underestimate the President at their own risk. He maintained that the APC remains focused on convincing voters that the reforms being implemented by the Tinubu administration deserve continuity beyond 2027. The former governor, who argued that President Tinubu deserves a second term, dismissed the ideas and plans being shared by opposition candidates. “What are the other parties offering that is different, that is better, that is compelling as a reason to interrupt the process of reform, growth, and restructuring that is already underway?” he asked. He also queried what he described as the opposition’s alternative message, asking, “What is the alternative message to what we are currently dealing with? What is the compelling message? Obi contested the 2023 presidential election, finishing third nationally behind APC candidate Tinubu and Atiku Abubakar under the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). However, he defeated Tinubu in Lagos State, where he secured 582,454 votes against the APC candidate’s 572,606. The APC has ruled the metropolitan state for 27 years. item.title: ‘Even A Tomato Seller Knows Strait Of Hormuz’, Fashola Blames Global Conflicts For Economic Pressures
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has defended the economic policies of President Bola Tinubu’s administration, arguing that global developments, including the COVID-19 pandemic, the Russia-Ukraine war and conflicts in the Middle East, have contributed to the cost-of-living challenges Nigerians are grappling with. Fashola, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria, said Nigeria was not insulated from global economic pressures, particularly disruptions to supply chains, energy supplies and food markets. Speaking during an appearance on Politics Today, the former Minister of Works said the global economy was still recovering from the effects of the pandemic, which disrupted economic activity and production worldwide. He explained that shortages of goods following the pandemic had pushed up prices, while the Russia-Ukraine war further affected the supply of major energy and food commodities, including diesel and wheat. This aerial photograph shows boats anchored off Oman’s northern Musandam Peninsula near the Strait of Hormuz on June 27, 2026. (Photo by – / AFP Fashola also identified the ongoing conflict in the Middle East as another factor affecting global markets, particularly energy supplies and shipping costs. “It’s also important to contextualise the factors and the circumstances that have exacerbated the cost-of-living challenges,” he said. “Even the tomato seller knows the Strait of Hormuz and prices his or her goods according to replacement costs now.” ‘Helping Families In Need’ Fashola, a former Minister of Works, also backed President Tinubu for a second term, defending the administration’s response to challenges. Defending the Tinubu administration’s response to economic pressures, Fashola listed the minimum wage review, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), tax reforms, and the introduction of compressed natural gas (CNG) as part of measures intended to ease the burden on Nigerians. He said the minimum wage review was one of the government’s early responses to the rising cost of living, aimed at putting more money in workers’ hands. President Bola Tinubu during the inauguration of the APC PCC. However, he argued that increasing wages alone could not address the problem, warning that continuously injecting cash into the economy could create what he described as “hyper-demand inflation”. Fashola said the government had also sought to address some of the major expenses that reduce household disposable income, including rent, transportation, healthcare and children’s education. He identified NELFUND as one of the interventions aimed at easing financial pressure on families by supporting students’ education. “Your disposable income goes to rent, goes to transport, and goes to health care, and goes to your children’s education. And NELFUND was, okay, we will help families in need,” he said. item.title: ‘Nothing Suggests To Me Tinubu Is Not Fit,’ Fashola Dismisses Health Concerns
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has dismissed concerns about President Bola Tinubu’s physical and mental fitness for office, saying he has seen nothing to suggest that the president is incapable of performing his duties. Fashola, a former Minister of Works and Housing, made the remarks on Tuesday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today , where he was asked whether he considered Tinubu physically fit to lead the country. “Nothing suggests to me that he’s not fit for it. Yes, he’s older. That doesn’t mean his mental capacity is gone. He’s still giving directives. And when I see him, he’s working. He’s still reading, authorising, minuting on things,” he said. President Bola Tinubu during his address to Nigerians for the 66th Independence Day anniversary on October 1, 2026. Questions about Tinubu’s health and physical condition have featured in public discussions since the 2023 presidential election campaign. During the campaign, concerns were raised by critics over his physical appearance, movements and stamina at public events. The debate continued after he assumed office in May 2023, with opposition figures and other critics occasionally questioning his capacity to discharge the responsibilities of the presidency. The concerns resurfaced in 2026 amid renewed scrutiny of his public appearances, including videos circulated online showing him moving cautiously at some events. The Presidency and the All Progressives Congress (APC) have repeatedly defended the president, maintaining that he is capable of carrying out his constitutional responsibilities. Tinubu has also dismissed speculation about his health. In September 2026, following an extended stay in Europe, he told reporters that he was ready to “work, walk and kick.” ‘More Mature’ The former governor, who worked closely with Tinubu during his eight-year administration in Lagos from 2007 to 2015, said the president had become more experienced over the years. Asked to compare the Tinubu he knew in the early 2000s with the president he knows today, Fashola said the president had become more mature. “Well, a much more mature one, certainly, without doubt. I am not the chief of staff he employed in 2002. That’s 39 years. I was 39 then. I’m 63 now. So we must give him that credit for the experience he has gained,” he said. ﻿ Fashola acknowledged that Tinubu might no longer maintain the same work routine he had in the past, particularly when it came to keeping late nights, but maintained that the president remained capable of handling demanding responsibilities. “Maybe not keeping late nights that he used to do. I’m not sure. He can still run the engine,” he added. item.title: ‘The Proposal Is Not Realistic,’ Fashola Faults Atiku’s Fuel Subsidy Reversal Plan
item.description: Former Minister of Works and Housing, Babatunde Fashola, has faulted the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar’s proposal to restore fuel subsidy if elected president in 2027, describing it as unrealistic and questioning the availability of crude oil to sustain the policy. Fashola said the proposal lacked sufficient explanation on how the country would secure the crude oil required to support domestic refineries and maintain a subsidy regime. The former Lagos State governor spoke on Tuesday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today , where he argued that Nigeria’s existing challenges with crude oil production, pipeline vandalism and insecurity raised questions about the feasibility of Atiku’s proposal. “If we have refineries working, what is our current oil quota? Are we optimising it yet? No, because they are legacy issues, challenges with security people, vandalism. So where is this magic crude oil going to come from? People are entitled to ask,” he said. Fashola added that Atiku needed to explain how he intended to implement the proposal, insisting that Nigerians should be allowed to assess its feasibility before deciding whether to support it. “If he can explain, good, let the people choose. But without proof, it is like abracadabra. Because the reality that will come then is that he will say that, ‘I didn’t know that there was not enough crude oil.’ That was what happened,” he added. ﻿ When asked whether his position was that Atiku’s proposal was feasible, Fashola replied: “The proposal is not realistic. I am looking at the proposal, not the personality. “In this environment, it is very easy to throw promises at people. When the rubber hits the road, reality sets in. First question is, in 2023, didn’t he see through this when he was making the promise to remove the subsidy? And that goes to a question of credibility. Those who believe at face value that promise, he will come back and tell you that, ‘Oh, I changed my mind. I didn’t think through it,’” he said. Fashola argued that restoring the subsidy would require more than a presidential declaration, noting that legislative backing would also be necessary. “Subsidy is not just about, ‘I said it.’ It will come down to the real economy, and legislators will have to repeal a law to say subsidy is now lawful. How many legislators are ready to stake their election on going back to subsidy? Those are the real issues,” he said. According to him, all the major presidential candidates in the 2023 election had promised to remove the subsidy, and Atiku needed to explain what had changed to justify his current position. “Is it because people are impacted? It’s true. But what are you going to do differently? Where are you going to find the money to sustain what you are offering? It’s not sustainable,” he said. item.title: Army Arrests Seven Suspects, Recovers 38 Phones, Mercedes-Benz In Plateau
item.description: Troops of Sector 1, Joint Task Force, Operation Enduring Peace, have arrested seven suspected criminals and recovered 38 mobile phones, a Mercedes-Benz E350, a motorcycle and other items in separate operations in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State. The spokesperson for the Joint Task Force, Captain Chinonso Oteh, disclosed this while presenting the suspects at the task force headquarters in Jos, where he gave details of the operations. According to the task force, the arrests followed intelligence-led operations conducted on November 6 and 10, 2026, as part of efforts to curb armed robbery, phone snatching and other criminal activities in the state. In the first operation, troops acted on a report of a phone-snatching incident involving a gunman. The report led to the identification of the location of the stolen phone at Prime House Hotel, along Ring Road, Jos North. A raid on the hotel resulted in the arrest of five suspects. Items recovered during the operation included 26 mobile phones, 27 phone pouches, three MP3 devices, two earpods, an HP laptop, a dagger, four power banks and a Mercedes-Benz E350 with registration number Plateau BBK-01NB. The task force said a further search of the suspects’ vehicle, after it was towed to the Sector 1 headquarters, led to the recovery of 12 additional mobile phones, bringing the total number of phones recovered in the operation to 38. In a separate operation on November 10, troops deployed at Naraguta, working with members of the Vigilante Group of Nigeria, arrested two more suspects during a routine patrol. The suspects were reportedly found with a suspected stolen Boxer motorcycle and a toy pistol. The task force said the seven suspects and the recovered items would be handed over to the Plateau State Police Command for further investigation and possible prosecution. The Commander of Operation Enduring Peace, Major General Maxwell Dangana, reaffirmed the task force’s commitment to combating crime and sustaining peace across its joint operations area. He said the task force would continue to rely on intelligence-driven operations and collaboration with other security agencies and local vigilante groups to tackle criminal activities. Dangana also urged residents to remain vigilant and provide credible and timely information to security agencies to support efforts to restore and sustain lasting peace in Plateau State.
